title: A Detention for the Playlist
premise: Paloma Reyes, the varsity team's statistician, has spent years proving with numbers what everyone refuses to see: the district's star players are being graded and scouted on a rigged curve that keeps certain kids invisible. When an anonymous group chat begins posting predictions — game scores, a teacher's resignation, even Paloma's own words — days before they happen, he realizes the chat is run by someone inside the system with access to the district's sealed data, and that the predictions are a countdown. As Paloma and the chat's reluctant members race to expose the rigging before the state championship seals the falsified records forever, Paloma falls for Marisol, the athletic director's daughter, whose loyalty to her father puts her on the other side of the truth. In the end, Paloma chooses truth over safety, testifying at the school board with the chat's final prediction — his own expulsion — hanging over him; the board overturns the records, Marisol stands with him at the cost of her father's career, and the chat goes silent, its last message reading simply: 'prediction fulfilled. your turn now.'
about_author: Rafael Iversen is a former high school math teacher who spent six years keeping scorebooks for a basketball team he slowly realized he couldn't cheer for honestly. He writes young adult novels about kids who do the arithmetic adults refuse to do, and he still can't watch a penalty kick without checking the stats.

chapters.title: Significant Digits
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He runs the numbers on the team's grading curve and finds a pattern too clean to be accidental, but files it away because everything is fine, obviously. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a person who trusts math more than people — and just felt math betray him.

chapters.title: The Group Chat With No Admin
chapters.summary: A chat invites itself onto Paloma's phone: six anonymous handles, no creator listed. Its first message predicts Friday's final score to the point. Paloma's POV; the beat is skeptical fascination curdling into unease when the score lands exactly.

chapters.title: Marisol Ochoa Has Nice Handwriting
chapters.summary: Paloma is caught erasing a whiteboard of suspicious numbers by Marisol, the athletic director's daughter and team manager, who covers for him without knowing why. Her POV. The beat: a spark of alliance between two people who both notice everything and say nothing.

chapters.title: Prediction Two: Coach Delgado Resigns
chapters.summary: The chat posts a resignation letter three days early; Coach Delgado quits with the exact wording, citing 'family reasons.' Paloma's POV. The beat: the shift from coincidence to pattern, and the first real fear that the chat knows things it shouldn't.

chapters.title: Who Else Is in the Room
chapters.summary: Paloma cross-references who had access to the district's sealed data server and narrows it to a handful of adults — including Marisol's father. Her POV. The beat: loyalty beginning to strain as she wonders what her dad keeps locked in his office.

chapters.title: The Rigged Curve, Explained
chapters.summary: Paloma lays out the fraud for the chat: certain players' stats and grades are inflated, others suppressed, all to feed a scouting deal that pays the district. His POV. The beat: righteous clarity — he finally has a shape for the wrongness he's felt for years.

chapters.title: Deniability
chapters.summary: The chat warns Paloma to stop digging: 'prediction: you get a detention you didn't earn.' He gets one that afternoon, on a fabricated charge. His POV. The beat: the machinery of the institution flexing, and Paloma realizing he's being managed.

chapters.title: Rooftop Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marisol finds Paloma serving his detention-adjacent cleanup duty and he shows her the rigged curve. Her POV. The beat: love against duty — she wants to believe her father, but the numbers don't lie, and neither, apparently, does Paloma.

chapters.title: Six Handles, One Liar
chapters.summary: Paloma deduces from typing rhythms and response times that two of the six chat members are the same person. His POV. The beat: paranoia sharpening into detective work; the enemy is inside the chat itself.

chapters.title: Prediction: The Injury
chapters.summary: The chat predicts that bench player Theo Vasquez will be injured in Friday's game — a 'clean' injury that conveniently ends his scholarship eligibility before anyone reviews his suppressed stats. Theo's POV. The beat: dread and defiance as Theo decides to play anyway.

chapters.title: Friday Night, Played as Predicted
chapters.summary: The game unfolds eerily close to the prediction; Theo goes down hard but walks off under his own power, breaking the script. Paloma's POV. The beat: hope — the future is predicted, not fixed.

chapters.title: My Father's Password
chapters.summary: Marisol, torn, uses her dad's home office to trace the chat's activity logs and finds her own handle among the six — created without her knowledge. Her POV. The beat: betrayal at its most intimate; she's been a puppet in someone's countdown.

chapters.title: The Countdown Revealed
chapters.summary: The chat's hidden archive shows every prediction was a countdown to one date: the state championship, after which the falsified records become permanently sealed. Paloma's POV. The beat: the stakes snap into focus — a deadline, not a mystery.

chapters.title: Labels Coming Off
chapters.summary: Paloma, Marisol, and Theo meet in person for the first time as the people behind their labels: the statistician, the director's daughter, the disposable kid. Alternating POVs. The beat: fragile solidarity forming out of shared damage.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: The athletic director offers Paloma a college recommendation and a clean record if he deletes the data and leaves the district quietly. His POV. The beat: temptation played straight — the easy out, priced exactly at his integrity.

chapters.title: What Marisol Chose
chapters.summary: Marisol confronts her father; he admits the scheme, framed as protecting the school, and asks her to stay silent for the family. Her POV. The beat: love against duty reaching its breaking point — she chooses truth, and loses the version of her father she loved.

chapters.title: Prediction: Expulsion
chapters.summary: The chat's final message predicts Paloma's expulsion, effective the Monday after the championship, signed with the district seal. His POV. The beat: cold terror — the countdown was always about him, and the clock is nearly out.

chapters.title: Stealing the Sealed Records
chapters.summary: Paloma, Marisol, and Theo break into the records office the night before the championship to copy the raw data. Theo's POV. The beat: fear transmuted into purpose; three invisible kids making themselves impossible to ignore.

chapters.title: State Championship
chapters.summary: The rigged final game plays out while Paloma waits to testify at an emergency board session scheduled by an anonymous tip — the chat's last gift. His POV. The beat: held breath; the two endings of his life running in parallel.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Paloma presents the raw data to the board as the chat predicts his own words in real time, exposing the final member: the district's data administrator, who built the chat to force someone else to do what she couldn't. Paloma's POV. The beat: the climax — truth spoken aloud, at full personal cost.

chapters.title: Prediction Fulfilled
chapters.summary: The board voids the sealed records and suspends the expulsion; Marisol's father resigns, and she stands beside Paloma in the empty gym after. Her POV. The beat: grief and love coexisting; justice arrived, but nothing is unbroken.

chapters.title: Your Turn Now
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the chat sends one final message to Paloma — the archived data, and 'prediction fulfilled. your turn now.' He forwards it to Theo and starts a new spreadsheet. Paloma's POV. The beat: resolution as inheritance — the work of justice outside the law continues, handed off.
